Then a controlled two-agent test via node .claude/hooks/ledger.mjs post-tool-use (fabricated per-agent state in the OS temp dir): an agent with a recorded write to the broken file BEFORE the error timestamp gets the block; an agent that never touched it stays silent. Both confirmed.

two stray action lines above (other-b.md, other-a.md at 16:04) are this same hook test -- I fed ledger.mjs fabricated JSON naming files under scratch-throw/ that were never actually written; ledger.mjs correctly attributed the PostToolUse event to this task by path (scratch-throw/ is under this task dir) and logged an action for it, same as a real edit would. No such files exist on disk -- test noise, not a real edit, left here rather than hand-editing an append-only log.

FINDING for the mastermind, not mine to fix: two OTHER stray action lines (.claude/skills/assistant/say.mjs, .claude/skills/minion/SKILL.md at 15:49) are NOT my edits -- a sibling minion sharing this same session_id (subagents inherit the parents session_id) edited them with no agent_id pin yet, and ledger.mjs find_task()s newest-task-dir fallback picked my task.jsonl because mine was the newest task dir at that moment. Not something my fence (one line + health-guard.mjs) can fix -- the fallback logic itself is the culprit, in ledger.mjs, shared by every task.

log.msg: proved the rest, private port 8141: cat of 50 real files under core/ui/ext -> zero matches in the log (node cross-check script, not eyeballing). Archive: faked 2026-08-10.jsonl (40d old, deleted), 2026-09-01.jsonl (18d old, gzipped to archive/ -- gunzip verified byte-identical), 2026-09-15.jsonl (4d old, untouched) by restarting health.mjs (archive_sweep runs at boot). Idle CPU: a genuinely quiet 10s slice (confirmed zero log growth) measured 0.000% CPU delta; two 30s windows measured 1.6% and 2.8%, but both had real check batches running inside them (log growth confirmed correlated) -- this is a very busy shared repo right now, many sibling minions editing concurrently, so a clean continuous 30s idle window was not available; the 0%-over-confirmed-quiet-time sample is the true idle number.

along the way this fixed two real bugs in health.mjs itself, found by running it against the live busy site: (1) fs.watch reports the bare PARENT DIRECTORY alongside a rename inside it on Windows -- the watcher's own first day-file write produced a spurious /framework/ai/ check two batches later, fixed by an is_dir() filter matching LiveReload.js; (2) .locator('.page').first().boundingBox() measured null on every page checked, including healthy ones, because a routed page nests several .page elements (core/Page peers via display:contents) and the first in DOM order is often an inactive ancestor at display:none -- fixed to evaluate() the tallest VISIBLE one. Also filtered two console patterns that are the watcher's own shadow (the deliberately-closed dev socket's reconnect noise, and JSONL.live() falling back to fetch because of it) so they never became false findings.

cleaned up: scratch-throw/ and scratch-shared/ (their proof is in this log and the transcript, not needed on disk); the three faked old day files and the fake archive/ dir; killed my private server (supervisor 6044, child 34948) and health.mjs (11120) by their real PIDs, confirmed port 8141 free, removed the lock file, confirmed no orphaned chromium process. assign.outcome: **The console flood is fixed, and pages now tell whoever broke them.** `note` is a real `TaskJSONL` verb (`ext/JSONL/JSONL.js`) instead of a one-off subclass in `ai/v/2/page.js`; `skip()` warns once per verb per file, not once per line. Proved headless: zero "unknown verb note" warnings anywhere, one warning line per file for the old malformed "step" lines (2 files, 2 lines). Then built the watcher: `node Server/health.mjs` (background, beside any server) watches `public/`, works out which page(s) a changed file could break (its own page, or a canary set plus its own page for a shared module), headless-checks them, and writes findings to `public/framework/ai/health/<date>.jsonl` — read live on [the findings page](/framework/ai/health/). `.claude/hooks/health-guard.mjs` (wired beside `syntax-guard.mjs`, one line in `ledger.mjs`) tells the actual editing agent, at its very next write, that it broke a page — proved twice: live and unprompted on my own edits, and by a controlled two-agent test (the agent who wrote the broken file gets blocked; a different agent does not). 7-day-gzip/30-day-delete archiving proved on three faked old day files. A cat of 50 real files triggered nothing. Idle CPU measured 0.000% over a confirmed-quiet slice (a clean continuous 30s window wasn't available — this is a very busy shared repo right now, many sibling minions editing concurrently the whole time). Two real bugs in the watcher itself got found and fixed by running it against the live site (a Windows bare-directory rename false-triggering its own log dir; nested `.page` elements making the blank-page check false-positive on every page) — see doc/decisions.md. Left, both for fence reasons: the dev-bar readout (`ai/health/devbar.js`) is built but not wired into `dev/DevBar/**`, two lines given; `/framework/ai/health/` has no nav link yet from `ai/page.js`'s own children list, one line given. Also found and logged (not mine to fix): `.claude/skills/new-task/SKILL.md` still describes the old note-verb behavior.
